page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6i-c24g1.6xlarge is a GPU-accelerated compute instance designed for machine learning inference and graphic workloads. Powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8163 processor, the instance provides 24 dedicated virtual CPUs across 12 physical cores on an x86_64 architecture, supported by 33 MB of L3 cache. It incorporates 93.0 GB of system memory (3.88 GB per vCPU) and features a dedicated NVIDIA Turing T4 GPU with 16 GB of VRAM. The instance includes an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, operates on a KVM hypervisor, and provides no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached cloud disks for persistent storage needs.

Benchmark evaluations reflect a profile optimized for GPU-centric processing rather than single-threaded CPU tasks. CPU benchmarks indicate modest single-thread performance, recording 935.0 on Geekbench single-core and 1107.39 on stress-ng, placing it in the lower quartile of modern CPU tiers. However, multi-core throughput remains steady across 24 vCPUs, yielding a PassMark CPU score of 18301.8 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 7397.0. The integrated NVIDIA T4 accelerator delivers high prompt-processing efficiency, reaching 8377.38 tokens per second on a small 135M parameter LLM and 1130.26 tokens per second on a medium 7B model, alongside 33.05 tokens per second for medium-model text generation.

From an efficiency standpoint, the hardware balance matches entry-to-midrange acceleration tasks where deploying expensive enterprise training accelerators would be underutilized. The instance trades per-core compute speed and integrated storage for economical tensor acceleration and balanced memory density. Workloads best aligned with the ecs.gn6i-c24g1.6xlarge include real-time deep learning inference, image recognition, video transcoding pipelines, lightweight graphics rendering, and batch inference workflows.

Hardware acceleration is provided by a single NVIDIA Turing T4 GPU with 16 GB of VRAM. The platform includes an 8 Gbps network baseline and relies entirely on remote storage, containing no local disks. Synthetic benchmarks indicate below-average single-core CPU throughput, but multi-threaded processing remains consistent with an 18301.8 PassMark CPU score. The NVIDIA T4 GPU excels in AI prompt processing, achieving 1130.26 tokens per second on a 7B parameter LLM and 8377.38 tokens per second on a 135M model. Given its resource profile, this server is suitable for deep learning model inference, video encoding, computer vision processing, and moderate graphical simulation workloads.
